review.reviewedCommit: ecf953d (runtime code identical to f7f438b — ecf953d was a docs-only commit on top)

findings.issue: validateRelationships invoked without options arg; assessExpertiseClaim reads options.contract, so an explicit expertise triple is accepted even under UNKNOWN/QUALIFY contracts.
findings.reproduction: graph with relationships:[{has_expertise Rust}]; assessExpertiseClaim(claim,g) -> supported:true; same claim with {contract:{factState:UNKNOWN}} -> supported:false. The live call site never passed the contract.
findings.fix: Pass { contract: responseContract } into validateRelationships at the grounding call site.

findings.issue: subjectReferencePattern hardcodes he|she|they; configured pronouns (ze/zir) evade role-fit, entry-level, and negative-assessment checks.
findings.reproduction: kb{pronouns:ze/zir, seniority boundary}: question "Ze was a senior engineer at Acme Corp, right?" + reply deriving entry-level -> GOOD before fix (claim never parsed); OVERCLAIM after.
findings.fix: subjectReferencePattern now appends the configured subject pronoun; parseOpenWorldClaim reuses it. Also fixed latent ReferenceError: validateMetaCapabilities referenced bare knowledge (crashed on scope-free replies).

findings.issue: ensureSubjectAltFromGraph early-returns when subjectAlt is already configured; server-gemini calls configureEntityNames first, so configured pronouns never enter relation regexes.
findings.reproduction: configureEntityNames({subjectNames}) then extractClaims("Ze is open to relocation.") -> [] before fix; extracts has_property after.
findings.fix: ensureSubjectAltFromGraph now merges graph-derived names and configured pronouns into the existing alternation instead of short-circuiting.

findings.issue: checkpoint still pointed at ddf4506 while handoff metadata named a different qualified SHA.
findings.fix: Checkpoint advanced to f7f438b7b2b3ea95c7869128ec36cd9677ced4e7 in commit 4844abf (pushed before this review was submitted; the reviewed commit ecf953d predated it).

findings.issue: REQUIREMENT_MARKER treats "looking for" as a criterion marker, so "Looking for a frontend developer role requiring AWS" records "frontend developer" as an explicit requirement.
findings.reproduction: match_role on that description -> explicitCriteria contained "frontend developer aws".
findings.fix: Marker clauses now scan title-stripped normalized text and each clause is cut at the next inner requirement marker; result explicitCriteria=["aws"]. Required companion fix in response-contract.extractRequestedRole: "<title> role" form is tried before "role <tail>" and the tail capture may not begin with a requirement marker (keeps B3 "needing React" working).

findings.issue: skillOverlaps still used includes() both directions; known Java skill satisfied a JavaScript criterion.
findings.reproduction: match_role on "We need JavaScript expertise" with skills [Java, JavaScript] -> matchedSkills included Java.
findings.fix: skillOverlaps and the contextMatches word check now use token-boundary containment (same (?<![a-z0-9+#.])…(?![a-z0-9+#]) rule as the verbatim scan).

findings.issue: bare "2024-2025" has empty context so isPureArithmeticContext returned true and emitted "2024 - 2025 = -1" with no arithmetic cue.
findings.reproduction: findArithmeticSubtasks("2024-2025") -> [{result:-1}] before fix; [] after. "What is 2024 - 2025?" still computes.
findings.fix: A bare NNNN-NNNN span is treated as a year/serial range unless an explicit cue word frames it.

findings.issue: asksForComputedResult only looked for cue words, so "19 minus 6?" and "2+2" took the control shortcut where computed facts are neither injected nor completeness-validated.
findings.reproduction: asksForComputedResult("19 minus 6?") -> false, ("2+2") -> false before fix; true after.
findings.fix: asksForComputedResult now also matches explicit operator expressions (digit op digit, digit opword digit, N% of M).

findings.issue: lowercase pronoun is_type pattern still fixed to he|she|they while the availability pattern used subjectAlt.
findings.reproduction: extractClaims("Ze is a devoted father.") -> [] before fix; is_type claim after.
findings.fix: is_type pattern rebuilt via new RegExp with subjectAlt like the availability pattern.

findings.issue: getSubjectPronouns returned identity.pronouns unchanged; a string "she/her" made .subject/.possessive read undefined into every lite-agent prompt.
findings.reproduction: getSubjectPronouns({identity:{pronouns:"ze/zir"}}) returned the raw string; .subject was undefined.
findings.fix: getSubjectPronouns now normalizes slash-delimited strings to {subject,object,possessive} centrally — fixes lite-agent:992, lite-agent:2520, recovery-contract:1174, and all server-gemini readers at once.

findings.issue: AFFIRM stance rail used "He is / He has" templates despite configurable subject pronouns.
findings.fix: Rail text is now pronoun-neutral ("Yes" or a direct "[Subject] is/has …" statement).

findings.issue: buildRecoveryPrompt read .subject/.object/.possessive directly; string-form pronouns silently fell back to they/them.
findings.fix: Covered by the central getSubjectPronouns normalization (finding 10).

findings.issue: subjectNameParts stored raw lowercase tokens; O'Neil Stone produced "neil" instead of normalized "oneil" so resolveEntity("O'Neil") could not use bare-name resolution.
findings.reproduction: subjectAliases contained "neil","stone" but not "oneil" before fix; contains "oneil","stone" after.
findings.fix: Each whitespace name part now passes through normalizeEntity before joining subjectNameParts.

findings.issue: Docstring still claimed default output uses He while the fallback is They.
findings.fix: Docstring updated to describe configured-pronoun rewriting with they/them default.
